Q: Is there a way to tie code to multiple GAS using clasp for testing? A:

Still no native solutions, but some workarounds are developing.

Clasp v2

  1. Storing multiple targets in the .clasp.json file was proposed in #349. It was closed in favour of the next option:
  2. The clasp setting command was added in #350. So now at least you can script it with something like clasp setting scriptId id1 && clasp push && clasp setting scriptId id2 && clasp push.
  3. Storing multiple targets in the .clasp.json file was again proposed in #625. It was closed in favour of the next option:
  4. Multi-developer workflow support was proposed in #991 and is still open. Personally I can't see how this would help anyway.
  5. Two entire node projects provide just this functionality. The latest is multi-clasp2.
  6. A hybrid of #1 and #2 is possible by creating multiple json files and cping them into place one at a time. Eg. (not tested) for f in *.clasp.json; do cp "$f" .clasp.json; clasp push; done
  7. As described in #350, switch to a "standalone" script instead of a "container bound" script. Container bound (attached to a particular document) scripts have more capabilities, but it turns out there are tricks to get a standalone script to act as a container bound script by specifying the scriptId.
    • This may have limitations (like complexity and speed?) that I haven't explored.

For me, #2 and #6 are pretty neck and neck. I went with #2 because it's just a single extra file, a deploy.sh. You could even replace the scriptId in the actual .clasp.json file is a dummy value, and replace it at the end of the deploy.sh, to keep the working copy clean and force the correct deploy method.

Clasp v3

Grr, all the guidance I found and documented above turns out to be associated with clasp v2. For v3, setting has gone. The best option now seems to be #6 above, which is simplified by the new --project flag.

First create multiple <id>.clasp.json files instead of the one .clasp.json file, where <id> is some unique identifier.

Then run a script like this to use each one in turn:

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Call `clasp push` for each of the clasp.json files
# to automatically push to multiple Google documents.
# Ref: https://stackoverflow.com/a/79996941/3697870

set -e
shopt -s nullglob

# Execute commands from the script directory.
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

for f in *.clasp.json; do
    set -x
    clasp --project "$f" push
    { set +x; } 2>/dev/null
done

Q: Debugging vLLM with debugpy on WSL fails: AttributeError: module 'ray' has no attribute 'is_initialized' A: 
Root cause: this is not a vLLM/debugpy-specific bug — it's a known Ray
circular-import issue that only triggers on WSL. In ray/python/ray/__init__.py
there's a WSL-only branch (detected via "microsoft" in platform.release())
that does:

    import ray._private.compat
    ray._private.compat.patch_psutil()

This runs while the `ray` package itself is still mid-initialization. If
anything causes `ray` to be re-imported or the import machinery to be
re-entered before __init__.py finishes running (which is exactly what
debugpy's import hooking triggers under WSL), Python hands back a
partially-initialized `ray` module object that doesn't have `is_initialized`
(or `_private`) set yet, hence the AttributeError.

You can reproduce the underlying mechanism without debugpy or vLLM at all,
purely on WSL:

    import ray
    import sys
    del sys.modules["ray"]
    import ray   # raises the same AttributeError on affected versions

This exact reproduction and root cause is confirmed by the Ray maintainers
(ray-project/ray#42653), and fixed via ray-project/ray#42871, which changes
the import from `import ray._private.compat` to
`from ray._private import compat` to avoid the circular import.

Fix / workaround:
1. Upgrade to a Ray release that includes PR #42871 — this is the real fix.
2. If you must stay on an older Ray, import and fully initialize `ray`
   (e.g. call `import ray; ray.init()`) *before* attaching debugpy /
   starting the debug session, so `ray/__init__.py` finishes running before
   any debugger-triggered re-import can interrupt it.
3. As a last resort, run without the debugger attached during the ray.init()
   call, then attach afterward.

Q: Why does BFD-ld create two separate read-only (R) LOAD segments instead of merging them? A:

What is the exact technical mechanism or constraint that prevents BFD-ld from merging these two R segments?

I don't know for sure, but I strongly suspect that the answer has to do with limitations of the libbfd library, which gives BFD-ld its name.

That library was originally written when COFF and A.OUT formats were common, and it is entirely inadequate for representing complicated formats, such as ELF.

Among other things, that shows in other BFD-based utilities (such as objdump) not being able to accurately display contents of ELF files. See this and this.

P.S.

The latest BFD-ld, which I just built from ToT: GNU ld (GNU Binutils) 2.47.50.20260821 still produces 2 separate R LOAD segments and 4 total LOAD segments.

Q: Should (double)(std::float16_t(1024) + std::float16_t(1025)) be 2048.0 or 2049.0? A:

It can be either value. An implementation is permitted but not required to represent intermediate expression results with wider precision. ([expr.pre]/6)

The values of the floating-point operands and the results of floating-point expressions may be represented in greater precision and range than that required by the type; the types are not changed thereby.

For GCC, there's the -fexcess-precision= option to control whether to use a wider precision.

Q: Multiple Tables or Single Table in PostgreSQL A:

Let's start backwards:

If image versions can be edited multiple times, does a self-referencing table become the more natural model?

Not just natural but necessary. You cannot represent a tree (of arbitrary-depth) without a self-referencing table.

Is separating originals and edited images into two tables considered over-engineering in this case?

No, you do want to distinguish them afaiu. Your edited images also have a edit_type which you'll need to store somewhere, this is absent from your single-table design.

Which approach would you recommend for a long-term, maintainable solution?

Use two tables, but don't duplicate columns; basically forming an inheritance scheme. An image has 0…N edited "child" images, an image "is" 0…1 edited image - no edit data means it's an original.

CREATE TABLE image(
  id int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  url text UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  name text,
  client_id int REFERENCES client,
  product_id int REFERENCES product, 
  created_at timestamptz
);
CREATE TABLE image_edit(
  id int PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES image,
  parent_id int REFERENCES image,
  type edit_type
);
CREATE INDEX ON image_edit (parent_id);

You can query this with a left join:

SELECT
  id,
  url,
  name,
  client_id,
  product_id,
  created_at,
  COALESCE(e.parent_id, id) AS original_image_id,
  e.parent_id AS parent_image_id,
  e.type AS edit_type,
  e IS NULL AS is_original
FROM image
LEFT JOIN image_edit e USING (id);

Q: How to solve Error: Invalid or corrupt jarfile A:

In your manifest you have defined your main class as com.HelloWorldTesting.Hello. Looking at your project tree I can see that the Hello.java class is on your source folder root and is not in the package com.HelloWorldTesting.

Try setting your main class like this: "Main-Class": "Hello"

Also you have a manifest file in your src folder and you are generating a manifest with gradle:

manifest {
    attributes(
            'Implementation-Title': 'Hello World',
            'Main-Class': 'Hello'
    )
}

Having multiple manifest files leads to this unexpected behaviour. Delete the manifest from your source folder, run gradle clean and the build should work after that.

Q: Errno::ENOENT: No such file or directory @ rb_sysopen - /tmp/ A:

Are you sure your config/aws.yml is in the right location and formed properly? Please check for all the references to it on your codebase.

When executing rake tasks the whole rails environment gets loaded. The error you mentioned arises if any file called by initializers or rake tasks doesn't exist or is not formed correctly.
